title: Delhi HC Transfers Case to Another Bench Over Advocate's Courtroom Conduct
case_name: Arjun Dev Bhatia v. State (NCT of Delhi) & Ors.
citation: W.P.(CRL) 3418/2026, order dated 3 November 2026 (Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora, J.)
card_summary: The Delhi High Court transferred a petition linked to a domestic violence complaint to another bench after an advocate repeatedly declared he was crying for the justice system and began to walk out mid-hearing. Justice Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora called the conduct reckless and rejected the apology as not genuine. The transfer left intact the interim directions on rent deposit and status quo over the flat.
card_tip: A lawyer's conduct during a hearing can get the matter moved to another bench on its own, apart from and regardless of how the underlying case is argued.
verification_notes: Core facts (advocate's remark and walkout, transfer order, date of 3 November 2026, Justice Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora, rejection of the apology) confirmed across Bar and Bench's report and the order itself (hosted as a PDF by Bar and Bench and separately uploaded by LiveLaw), with CourtBook's report corroborating the same facts. The underlying dispute concerns possession of a flat and a domestic violence complaint pending before a Mahila Court in Rohini; the card does not state disputed details of the landlord-tenant relationship, which sources describe with minor variation.
